static_traits.name: Lin Feng
static_traits.family_status: Living alone,Living with a pet dog
static_traits.social_status: Has several close friends to talk with, but has not yet discussed writing-related issues with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy; occasional self-doubt in past writing but not as strong as now
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to identify and state automatic thoughts; skeptical of intervention but willing to try; fairly cooperative; concrete emotional descriptions (anxiety, hopelessness); fairly logical

basic_info.main_problem: I am experiencing writing-related failure and self-doubt. I think my last novel was written very poorly, and I worry I will never be able to write a decent work again.
basic_info.core_demands: These negative thoughts have begun to affect my writing motivation and overall mental health, so I decided to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: After the last novel was completed (about 6 months ago), the client had high expectations for the work but ultimately met with poor reviews and sluggish sales, so the client views the work as a failure, with ensuing and gradually worsening self-doubt and catastrophizing; since then, every time sitting down to write or thinking of writing triggers strong anxiety and self-denial, leading to procrastination or reluctant writing with dissatisfaction at the results.

In earlier writing experience, the client's first several works received good reviews and awards, and the client was recognized as a capable author; yet in the current predicament, the client often attributes these past successes to 'luck', finding it hard to internalize them as stable evidence of ability.

core_beliefs: I am destined to never write a decent work again

special_situations.event: Poor reviews and sluggish sales after the last novel's release
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the work does not yet achieve external praise and market recognition, it means I am a failed writer
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forces oneself to keep writing to prove ability, setting higher expectations and pressuring oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My works are all trash, I can never write good works again

special_situations.event: Every time sitting down to write or starting a new project
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail again, it proves I have no talent, and continuing to write is just a waste of time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Procrastination and avoidance kick in, or reluctant writing amid strong anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will fail again; this is a complete waste of time

special_situations.event: When seeing less-than-ideal comments about the work or recalling bad reviews
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the reviews are poor, others will think I am terrible, and my writing has no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding talking about writing in socializing situations, not discussing writing issues with friends to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They all think I write terribly and consider me unworthy of being called a writer

special_situations.event: Recalling past experiences of winning awards and receiving praise
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past successes do not show I am capable; that was just luck
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive evidence, staying immersed in self-criticism to maintain 'caution'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My past good results were just luck and cannot be replicated

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a talented writer, preserving the value of creation and self-esteem
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being negated, worrying about losing the identity and meaning of being a writer
defense_goal: Staying self-enclosed to avoid criticism or negation
Through procrastination and avoidance, reduces the risk of failing again
Through forcing oneself to write and self-reproach, maintains a sense of control and the illusion that 'effort equals safety'

object_relations.object_representation: Harsh reviewers and readers (critics ready to negate at any time)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests recording automatic thoughts and practicing restructuring, exploring alternative perspectives
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these thoughts 'are a part of who I am', change is hard or even impossible (treating current cognitions as self-evident reality)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Respond to their doubts in a gentle, accepting tone, emphasizing the safety and controllability of gradual attempts; use concrete, actionable small steps to invite experimentation rather than forcing persuasion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes past successes and awards, trying to balance the current conclusion with positive evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing past successes to 'luck', thereby weakening the impact of positive evidence and maintaining the current self-denial framework
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Stay empathic and curious, invite concretization of the process elements behind success (effort, skill, details of reader feedback), gently challenge the 'luck' interpretation with open-ended questions, and link it to replicable ability.

manifestations: Viewing writing as 'trash', questioning the value and identity of being a writer
Past successes are explained as luck, hard to internalize as meaning and ability
Has lost motivation and interest in the once-loved rock climbing activity
outcomes: Productivity drops markedly, overall mental health impaired

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Self-imposed rigid standard: the work must gain good reviews and sales, otherwise it is a failure
Using absolutist expressions like 'must' and 'forever' in cognitions (e.g. 'I will never write a decent work')

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not discussing writing troubles with close friends, turning instead to self-digestion and self-criticism
Choosing procrastination or forcing oneself to write under strong anxiety, replacing seeking support with self-pressure

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-denial ('my works are all trash'), excessive focus on potential failure which limits action
Holds strong skepticism toward counseling suggestions, finds new perspectives hard to accept but still tries carefully

positive_force: Past works have received praise and awards, with a foundation of writing ability and experience
Willing to try recording and restructuring automatic thoughts, can accept small-step experiments
Having some social support (several close friends to confide in, though writing troubles not yet discussed)
negative_force: Significant cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization and jumping to conclusions (predicting the future, mind reading)
Highly dependent on external evaluation, prone to personalizing bad reviews as low self-worth
Self-denial leads to procrastination and avoidance; compulsive writing intensifies anxiety and hopelessness

target_behavior.behavior: Strong anxiety and self-doubt arising in writing-related situations, with procrastination/avoidance of starting
antecedent: Thinking about starting a new project
Recalling the last novel's failure and bad reviews
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic anticipation of failure and negation, black-and-white standards and overgeneralization, stemming from the last novel's poor reviews and sales and dashed high expectations
target_behavior.function: Avoiding failure and negative evaluation to temporarily relieve anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Writing productivity drops markedly; overall mental health is impaired; motivation for activities once enjoyed (such as rock climbing) is lost

target_behavior.behavior: Forcing oneself to write amid strong anxiety (overexertion)
antecedent: When automatic thoughts like 'my works are all trash' and 'I will never write good works' arise
When facing writing tasks and deadlines
target_behavior.core_reason: Compensatory strategies adopted to fight the core belief of 'incompetence/failure', trying to prove self-worth through control and effort
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain a sense of control and self-validation, undoing feelings of powerlessness and failure
target_behavior.consequence: Anxiety and intensifying self-doubt, dissatisfaction with output, further consolidating negative beliefs and the avoidance cycle
